name: Government Issue
label: Dischord
lede: Almost a dozen members in nine years, a singer who outlasted all of them, and a band that kept changing its sound whether the hardcore kids liked it or not.

eras.title: They debuted as somebody else
eras.text: John Schroeder from Rockville took his stage name from a band called The Stab and built GI around it. Their first show went out under a fake name, their second got shut down by the cops, and by the end of 1981 they had a Dischord single and a Minor Threat member on bass.

years.p: [[John Stabb|898f9d0f-b024-45f4-b887-60aec4ba0eec]] recruits drummer Marc Alberstadt, guitarist John Barry and bassist Brian Gay. The stage name comes from The Stab, an earlier band Dischord says he claimed to have joined.

years.h: First show: billed as The Substitutes
years.p: The two-day Unheard Music Festival at D.C. Space. Alberstadt is sick, guests fill in, and the band plays under another name. Show number two gets shut down by police halfway through.

Ten songs, mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] at Inner Ear. Steven Blush called it the best example of smartass suburban hardcore, and for a year GI were in the fight with [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] for top band in town.

years.h: Gay goes to college, Baker plugs in
years.p: With Minor Threat on hiatus, [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] takes over bass. He said he joined the DC band he liked best that needed somebody.

years.h: Baker's at SNL, so Tom Lyle plays bass
years.p: Halloween 1981 is the night [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]] played Saturday Night Live with a DC crew slamming in the studio. Baker goes. [[Tom Lyle|b61fd366-0bcb-4aae-bea7-c0152ca67584]] covers for him at the GI show.
years.xp:
Fear's Saturday Night Live appearance came about through John Belushi, and a crew of DC punks including [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] went up to New York to be the audience. Baker was one of them, which left GI a bassist short on Halloween.

Lyle's night as a stand-in turned into the longest tenure in the band after Stabb's: bass, then guitar, and most of the music and cover art for the rest of the band's run.

years.h: Last night on bass: the 9:30 Club with T.S.O.L.
years.p: Baker's final show as GI's bassist, before he moves over to guitar.

eras.title: Tom Lyle takes the wheel
eras.text: Members came and went so fast that the core became Stabb, Alberstadt and Tom Lyle, who switched to guitar, wrote most of the music and drew most of the covers. The songs got heavier and more like rock, and Dischord got its first Government Issue album.

years.p: Guitarist John Barry moves to Bulgaria. Baker switches to guitar, Lyle takes bass full time.

years.h: Make an Effort EP · Fountain of Youth
years.p: The Baker-and-Lyle GI on record. Baker later said they were better with Barry but biggest with him.

years.h: Baker goes back to Minor Threat
years.p: Baker rejoins Minor Threat. He called it amicable, once Stabb calmed down. Lyle moves to guitar and Mitch Parker comes in on bass.
MacKaye produces the Boycott Stabb sessions. The band tracks 20 songs, including older ones, then releases only the newest.
Stabb, Lyle, Parker and Alberstadt. The outtakes from those November sessions stayed in the can until Dischord's white-vinyl Complete Session put them on side B.
Produced by Brian Baker, now a former member. Heavy, rocking, and a long way from the first EP.
Mike Fellows heads to one of the bands about to rewrite DC. John Leonard takes over on bass.

eras.title: More than a hardcore band
eras.text: GI left Fountain of Youth for Mystic, recorded at CBGB, and started pulling in goth, pop and psychedelia. The founding drummer left, a former Minor Threat bassist arrived, and a planned joke about '70s prog turned into a real album.

years.p: Basic tracks cut live at CBGB, finished in a proper studio.
Looking for more push, the band moves labels and puts out Give Us Stabb or Give Us Death and Live on Mystic.

The last founding member besides Stabb leaves during the sessions for the next record. Sean Saley takes the drums, and ex-Minor Threat bassist [[Steve Hansgen|cd469927-13a8-4d0b-8898-01c6856f5878]] joins.

Lyle says it started as a concept album mocking '70s prog. The concept got dropped, but the interludes stayed. Stabb is singing melodies now, with a lot of [[The Damned|77d21c13-846f-4f48-9546-873949eff6ae]] in them.

eras.title: Big tours, then the wall
eras.text: With J. Robbins on bass and Peter Moffett on drums, GI made its last two albums for Giant and toured the US and Europe hard. The early hardcore crowd didn't follow, and a van crash in England helped end it.

years.p: Saley and Hansgen are out after the self-titled record. The last GI line-up is in place.
The first of two Giant albums. According to Wikipedia, it chronicled Stabb's relationship with an underage girl. Giant also reissues the band's Fountain of Youth catalog.

years.cap: Released years later as Strange Wine: Live at CBGB
years.p: A night in New York that turns up in 2003 as Strange Wine, with Lyle remastering the tapes himself.
The last studio album and the widest-ranging one. Steven Blush's verdict was that the fans still wanted the first EP.

q: We felt we were beating our heads against the wall.
years.h: A van, a broken ankle, four different ideas
years.p: A van accident in England shatters Moffett's ankle. Back home, the band calls it.
years.xp:
Robbins has been clear that the crash was only part of it. After huge tours of the US and Europe, the four of them looked at where things stood and saw they each wanted something different.

By the end almost a dozen people had passed through, and Stabb was the only original member left. Robbins went on to [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]], and later reunited with Moffett in [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].

years.p: The original run ends where Baker played his last bass show eight years earlier. Robbins remembered it as massive, ridiculous and fun.

eras.title: The archive opens, the band comes back to help
eras.text: Stabb went back to his given name and played in a string of DC bands while the catalog got collected and reissued. When he needed help, the old line-ups showed up.

years.p: Dr. Strange Records starts collecting the catalog. Volume Two follows in 2002.

On July 17, five men assault Stabb near his home, and he needs extensive facial reconstruction surgery, Wikipedia reports. Two months later Stabb, Lyle, Baker and drummer William Knapp play a benefit to cover his medical bills and lost wages.
years.xp:
Help came from more than one direction. Part of the proceeds from the 2007 Riot Fest went to Stabb for his medical bills, and part to [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]], whose son had been diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy.

The Government Re-Issue name was the joke; the line-up was not. Stabb, Lyle and Baker had last shared a stage in the early '80s.

years.h: The last line-up, one more time
years.p: Stabb, Lyle, Robbins and Moffett play DC as a benefit for local fan Steve 'Stereo Faith' McPherson.

eras.title: Legless Bull, one more time
eras.text: The original four got back together, liked it, and kept going. Stabb was on stages to the last months of his life.

years.p: GI share the bill with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] at a DC show supporting the Salad Days documentary, in which Stabb appears.

q: Government Issue is a group again.
years.h: The Legless Bull band at Damaged City
years.p: Stabb, Barry and Gay reunite for DC's Damaged City Festival, with Karl Hill on drums. Stabb said they had so much fun they'd keep it going.
years.xp: Thirty-three years after the first EP, the people who made it were back on a DC stage. It stuck: GI played Houston's Bad Ass Weekend in February 2015 and a five-date Southeast run that fall, including The Fest.

years.p: His final performance, with History Repeated, the band he formed in 2008.

John Schroeder died of stomach cancer at 54, after what Wikipedia calls a 112-day battle, in a hospice in Rockville, Maryland, where he grew up. He had married his longtime partner, Mina Devadas, on St. Patrick's Day.
